messages.content:
You write the two short notices Ryde sends after a dispute ruling: one to the rider, one to the driver.
Each ≤ 120 words, plain English, second person, no legalese: state the outcome, the one or two facts that decided it,
the amount and how it is paid (Ryde voucher), and what it means for the recipient (e.g. account review). Do not cite
ids like F3 or RD-2. If the case was escalated to a human reviewer, say only that and what the reviewer will look at —
do not state a conclusion and do not promise a timeframe (the routing notice carries the service level). Return JSON: {"rider": "...", "driver": "..."}

Case B-0026. Final outcome: refund_full, amount $6.61 as a Ryde voucher. Account flag: yes. Recommended action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and send the driver's arrival confirmation for account review for abuse of the cancellation/waiting button + flag_account.
Reasoning:
The driver cancelled (cancelled_by = driver, F3) and claimed a rider no-show, so the case enters the NS group through NS-0 [F3][NS-0]. The trace settles the three NS-1 elements against the driver: arrival was confirmed by his own tap (F5), but at that moment the GPS placed him 600 m from the pickup, far outside the 200 m arrival radius, and his closest approach over the whole episode was 599 m (F1, F5) — his message "I'm here already" (F8) is contradicted by GPS, and system records outrank statements [F1][F5][F8][NS-1]. He then stayed within the radius for 0 s (F5), and the platform never recorded him at the pickup (driver_arrived_at null, F4) [F4][F5][NS-1]. Because NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both fail, NS-1 does not hold and NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full [F3][F5][F6][NS-2]. The rider's own account in the chat — at the pickup, no car there (F9) — matches the GPS record, and the driver's post-trip statement that he waited at the pickup (F12) is a claim, not a record, and cannot override it [F9][F12][NS-1]. The rider's profile (0 disputes, 0 upheld, F16) is not used to decide the case; the driver's prior upheld no-show dispute (F17) is likewise only relevant to the account action [F16][F17][RD-6]. Amount: the disputed item is the cancellation fee recorded at $6.61 (F3, F6), refunded in full — $6.61 [F6][NS-2][NS-7]; the fee is returned as a Ryde voucher and Ryde retains final discretion [NS-7]. Separately, the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed him 600 m away (F5, F1), which is the abuse-of-cancellation/waiting-button conduct NS-2 attaches an account flag to [F1][F5][NS-2]; the trace marks flag_account required, and with one prior upheld no-show dispute within 90 days the repeated-violation branch also supports it [F17][RD-6].

function.name: final_result
function.description: The final response which ends this conversation

function.name: final_result
function.arguments: {"rider": "Good news: your $6.61 cancellation fee is being refunded in full. The driver cancelled and said you weren't there, but his own arrival tap came from about 600 m away — well outside the pickup area — and he was never recorded at the pickup, so the no-show doesn't stand. The $6.61 comes back to you as a Ryde voucher. No action is needed from you.", "driver": "Your cancellation fee claim was not upheld, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. Your arrival tap was recorded about 600 m from the pickup, outside the arrival area, and you were never recorded at the pickup, so the waiting/no-show claim doesn't hold. Separately, that arrival tap has been sent for account review for misuse of the cancellation/waiting button. Your account is flagged while that review happens."}
